sandhi.rule: ङमो ह्रस्वादचि ङमुण्नित्यम् (8.3.32) does not apply
sandhi.note: After the long ā the final n is not doubled; it simply joins the next vowel. The same in सकलानभीष्टान्.
Final t (d) becomes the nasal n before the nasal n: विपन्नराणाम्. Not the participle विपन्न: read न विपत् नराणाम्.
Final m joins the vowel; -āḥ before the voiced h loses its visarga (ru → y, dropped before a consonant); the i of हि becomes y before ā: ह्याश्रयताम्.

samasa.vigraha: न विद्यते शेषः येषां ते, तान्
samasa.literal: those of which no remainder exists

morph.note: Present second singular of अप + √हन्: हन् + सि → हंसि, the n becoming anusvāra before s inside the word. With अप ‘away’: ‘you strike away, remove’. It governs both lines: रोगान् … अपहंसि, and (अपहंसि) कामान्.
Past participles of intransitive roots used in the active sense, with the force of a conditional: तुष्टा ‘(you,) when pleased’, रुष्टा ‘when angry’.
Abstract noun in -ता on आश्रय ‘refuge’: ‘refuge-hood’. With प्रयान्ति: ‘they attain the state of being a refuge’, i.e. they become a shelter for others.
विपद् is a root noun (वि + √पद् ‘to fall apart’) with no visible affix; its final d is pronounced t at a pause, so the padaccheda gives विपत्.

mantras.anvaya: (हे देवि, त्वं) तुष्टा (सती) अशेषान् रोगान् अपहंसि, रुष्टा तु सकलान् अभीष्टान् कामान् (अपहंसि)। त्वाम् आश्रितानां नराणां विपत् न (भवति)। त्वाम् आश्रिताः हि आश्रयतां प्रयान्ति।
mantras.anvaya_en: Two balanced clauses with one verb (अपहंसि), conditioned by तुष्टा and रुष्टा; then two statements about those who take refuge in her.
mantras.lit: Pleased, you strike away diseases without remainder; but angered, all longed-for desires. For men who have taken refuge in you there is no calamity; those who have taken refuge in you indeed attain the state of being a refuge.
mantras.tr: Pleased, you take away every illness; angered, every cherished hope. No misfortune befalls those who take refuge in you; those who take refuge in you become a refuge themselves.
mantras.tr_note: ‘become a refuge’ renders आश्रयतां प्रयान्ति ‘attain refuge-hood’.

comm.t: The hymn returns to the long metre of its opening stanzas (11.2–6; here indravajrā, eleven syllables a line). The first half sets out her power over fortune: her pleasure removes disease, her anger removes everything one longs for. The second half states the reward of refuge: no calamity, and more — the one who takes refuge becomes a refuge.

Traditionally this stanza is recited on its own as a prayer for freedom from illness. The last line is read as the fruit of devotion: the devotee’s protection reaches beyond himself to those who in turn depend on him.

Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) calls her भवरोगघ्नी (name 842), ‘destroyer of the disease of worldly existence’, and रोगपर्वतदम्भोलिः (name 748), ‘a thunderbolt to the mountain of disease’. The idea is shared; the works are separate.
A modern reading: refuge is not only received but passed on. Those who are held become able to hold others.

sandhi.note: Final t before the unvoiced k stays t; the words are only written together. Final m becomes anusvāra before a consonant.
ā + a → ā. The same in कृत्वाम्बिके and कान्या.
After ai (not a or ā) the visarga, as ru, stays r before a vowel and before a voiced consonant.
ā + ā → ā. The Gita Press writes a double avagraha (ऽऽ) to show that the long ā of आत्म- has merged into the ā of बहुधा; it is silent.

samasa.type: upapada tatpuruṣa (द्विष् = √द्विष् with the zero affix क्विप्)
samasa.sense: the enemies of the right order

morph.note: Passive construction with the past participle: एतत् यत् कदनं त्वया कृतम् ‘this slaughter which was done by you’; the agent stands in the instrumental.
Present third singular of प्र + √कृ (tanādi: करो-ति, strong stem करो-). In a rhetorical question: ‘who else does that?’ — no one.
Adverb of manner from बहु with the taddhita -धा (‘in … ways’), as द्विधा ‘in two’, सहस्रधा ‘in a thousand ways’.

mantras.anvaya: हे देवि अम्बिके, अनेकैः रूपैः आत्ममूर्तिं बहुधा कृत्वा त्वया अद्य धर्मद्विषां महासुराणां यत् एतत् कदनं कृतम्, तत् का अन्या प्रकरोति?
mantras.anvaya_en: A relative clause in the passive (यत् … कदनं त्वया कृतम्), with the absolutive phrase (रूपैः … कृत्वा) giving the means; the main clause is a rhetorical question resuming it with तत्.
mantras.lit: This slaughter of the great asuras, haters of dharma, which was wrought by you today, O Devī, having made your own body manifold through many forms — O Ambikā, what other (woman) does that?
mantras.tr: Today, Devī, you made your own form manifold in many shapes and wrought this slaughter of the great asuras who hated dharma. Ambikā, who else could do such a thing?
mantras.tr_note: The passive is turned active; the rhetorical present प्रकरोति is rendered ‘could do’.

comm.t: The gods recall the battle of chapters 8–10: the Devī appeared as many — the Mātṛkās, Kālī, Śivadūtī — and destroyed the asuras. No other being could have done it.

The stanza answers Śumbha’s taunt that she fought ‘relying on the strength of others’ (10.3 अन्यासां बलमाश्रित्य). The Devī had replied that the many forms were her own powers and drew them back into herself: एकैवाहं जगत्यत्र द्वितीया का ममापरा (10.5), ‘I alone am here in the world; who else is there besides me?’, and ‘I stood here in many forms by my power’ (10.8 अहं विभूत्या बहुभिरिह रूपैर्यदास्थिता). The gods’ question का अन्या echoes her own द्वितीया का.
A modern reading: plurality here is not division. The many forms are one power acting in many ways.

sandhi.note: u before the unlike vowel ā becomes v. The printed line breaks inside the word (विवेकदीपे- / ष्वाद्येषु); the word belongs to the first line.
The t of the pronoun stem त्वत् becomes d before a vowel.

sandhi.note: -e + a: the a is absorbed (avagraha). Inside the compound, महा + अन्धकार → महान्धकार.
i before e becomes y; the final t of एतत् becomes d before the vowel of अतीव.

samasa.sense: in what illuminates the power to distinguish the real from the unreal
samasa.alt: Also a karmadhāraya of metaphor (विवेकः एव दीपः, ‘discernment, which is a lamp’). It may stand as a third item of the list (‘in the lamps of discernment’) or in apposition to आद्येषु वाक्येषु (‘in the primal sayings, which are lamps of discernment’). The second is taken here; the first is equally grammatical.

samasa.sense: anyone besides you (अन्य takes the ablative)

samasa.type: karmadhāraya (rūpaka: the pit that is possessiveness)
samasa.sense: in the abyss of attachment to ‘me and mine’
samasa.alt: Also a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa, ममत्वस्य गर्तः ‘the pit of possessiveness’; the sense is the same.

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (qualifying ममत्वगर्ते); अतिमहत् is a prādi tatpuruṣa (अतिशयेन महत्)
samasa.literal: in which there is exceedingly great darkness
samasa.alt: It may also be a karmadhāraya (अतिमहान् अन्धकारः) in a second locative, ‘in the very great darkness’, parallel to ममत्वगर्ते.

morph.note: Causative of √भ्रम् ‘to wander, whirl’: the root vowel takes vṛddhi before -अय- (भ्रम् → भ्रामय-), ‘makes wander’; with वि ‘astray, about’. Its subject is का त्वदन्या, third person — so the question of the second line runs on into the second half: ‘who but you makes this world whirl?’.
ममत्व is an abstract noun in -त्व formed on मम, the genitive ‘of me, mine’: ‘mine-ness’, possessiveness. Abstracts formed on a case-form are rare and expressive.
अति + इव fused (अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः, 6.1.101) into one adverb, ‘exceedingly’.

mantras.anvaya: विद्यासु शास्त्रेषु विवेकदीपेषु आद्येषु वाक्येषु च त्वदन्या का (वर्तते)? अतिमहान्धकारे ममत्वगर्ते एतत् विश्वम् अतीव (त्वदन्या का) विभ्रामयति?
mantras.anvaya_en: One rhetorical question (का त्वदन्या) governs both halves: in the first it is the subject of an understood ‘is’ with five locatives; in the second it is the subject of विभ्रामयति.
mantras.lit: In the branches of knowledge, in the śāstras, in the primal sayings that are lamps of discernment — who is there other than you? (Who other than you) makes this universe whirl exceedingly in the pit of possessiveness, of very great darkness?
mantras.tr: In all knowledge and every scripture, in the ancient words that are lamps of discernment, who is there but you? And who but you sets this whole world whirling in the dark abyss of ‘mine’?
mantras.tr_note: The question का त्वदन्या is carried into the second half, as the third-person verb requires.

comm.t: Two sides of one power. The Goddess is present in every source of knowledge and discernment; and it is she who sends the world whirling in the darkness of possessiveness. The same question, ‘who but you?’, covers both.

The teaching is Medhas’s in the first chapter: creatures are thrown ‘into the whirlpool of mine-ness, the pit of delusion’ (1.53 ममतावर्त्ते मोहगर्ते निपातिताः) by the power of Mahāmāyā, who drags even the minds of the wise into delusion (1.55–56) and is also the supreme knowledge that frees (1.57). The ‘primal sayings’ are commonly understood as the Vedas. The question का त्वदन्या was asked in the gods’ hymn of chapter 4 as well (4.17).

Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) holds both sides in two names: विश्वभ्रमणकारिणी (name 889), ‘she who makes the universe whirl’, and ममताहन्त्री (name 165), ‘destroyer of possessiveness’. The texts are separate; the paired idea is shared.
A modern reading: the pit is ‘mine’. What darkens the world in this stanza is not ignorance of facts but the habit of possession.

flags.uncertain: Interpretive: विवेकदीपेषु may be a separate locative of the list or stand in apposition to आद्येषु वाक्येषु; अतिमहान्धकारे may be a bahuvrīhi qualifying ममत्वगर्ते or a parallel locative. The sense hardly changes.
